subject: Clarifying retention handback & subprocessor onboarding for US privacy annex
messages:
From: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
To: privacy@brightlinehealth.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 09 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarifying retention handback & subprocessor onboarding for US privacy annex

Hi Brightline privacy team (and Matthew),

Thanks again for the follow-up on the US privacy annex. We're close but have a few open points from procurement and engineering that we'd like to confirm so we can finalize the annex and start the DocuSign flow:

1) Retention handback trigger: Brightline asked for a technical "export and handback" for certain deletion/exit scenarios. Can you confirm the exact trigger you expect (e.g., customer-initiated deletion vs contract termination vs regulatory request)? Also, do you expect a single consolidated export or periodic handback snapshots?

2) Subprocessor onboarding timeline: procurement requested a committed notice period for new subprocessors and a minimal onshore fallback lead time if a subprocessor is unavailable. Is 30 days notice + 45 days onshore fallback acceptable? If not, please propose your preferred window.

3) Service provider vs processor language: we reviewed the draft annex and want to avoid any downstream resale classification that would conflict with our operating model. We propose the annex use the phrase "Service Provider (as defined under applicable US state privacy laws)" and include explicit limited-use restrictions. Any concerns?

I've attached an updated annex with inline comments (Brightline_US-Privacy-Annex_v2.pdf) and a current subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessors_20261109.csv). If it's helpful I can propose a short clause for the retention handback and the subprocessor notice that you can review.

Would appreciate confirmation by EOD Wednesday (11/11) to keep the launch timeline intact.

Thanks,
Nikhil Sharma
Head of Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference

From: Matthew Kline <matthew.kline@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: privacy@brightlinehealth.com
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 11:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying retention handback & subprocessor onboarding for US privacy annex

Hi Nikhil,

Thanks for the clear summary and the attachments — confirmed we received them. A few quick clarifications from our side: 

- Trigger: Our procurement/ops folks want two explicit triggers: (a) customer-requested deletion (including account-level termination) and (b) contract termination (end of term or breach). For (a) we expect a 30-day export window; for (b) we expect a one-time consolidated export within 60 days unless otherwise agreed.

- Format: CSV/JSON plus schema mapping is fine. Encryption-at-rest and signed checksum required for exports.

- Subprocessor notice: 30 days notice is acceptable for most subprocessors. For any subprocessor that handles persistent personal data outside the US we will need an "onshore fallback" plan within 45 days. That's consistent with what you proposed.

- Classification: We are comfortable with the "Service Provider (as defined...)" label but need an explicit sentence preventing resale or commercial use beyond the services described.

Procurement will want a short handback SLA and a statement on auditability (log exports for the export operation). I'll loop legal on Wednesday; if you can provide a clause we can review quickly that would help.

Best,
Matt
VP, Legal Ops
Brightline Health

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Nikhil Sharma <nikhil_sharma@redwood.ai>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Nov 2026 08:25:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Clarifying retention handback & subprocessor onboarding for US privacy annex

Nikhil —

Quick take from contracts/engineering: we should provide two short, testable snippets — one for the retention/handback SLA and one for subprocessor notice/fallback. Keep them intentionally scoped. Proposed language below that should satisfy procurement and legal review: 

1) Retention/handback (proposed):
"Upon Customer's deletion request or upon contract termination, Redwood Inference will provide a consolidated export of Customer Data (in CSV/JSON as agreed) within the timeframe below: (a) Customer-initiated deletion: export provided within 30 calendar days; (b) Contract termination: export provided within 60 calendar days. Export files will be encrypted (AES-256), accompanied by SHA-256 checksums, and made available via secure transfer. Redwood will retain a tamper-evident log of the export operation for 180 days for audit purposes."

2) Subprocessor notice/fallback (proposed):
"Redwood will provide Customer with at least thirty (30) calendar days' written notice prior to engaging any new subprocessor that will access Customer Data. For any subprocessor that results in transfer of persistent personal data outside the United States, Redwood will implement an onshore fallback plan within forty-five (45) calendar days of Customer's written request, which may include migration to an onshore provider or additional contractual safeguards. Redwood will not resell Customer Data or use it for commercial purposes beyond the Services agreed in the DPA."

If that looks okay I can drop these into the annex and send directly to Matt.

-Aditya
Director, Contract Strategy
Redwood Inference

Matt —

Thanks, appreciate the quick reply. I've incorporated Aditya's proposed snippets into the annex and attached the redlined PDF (Brightline_US-Privacy-Annex_v2.pdf). The key additions are the export SLA language (30/60 days), the encryption + checksum requirement, and the 30-day subprocessor notice + 45-day onshore fallback clause. We also included the non-resale sentence you requested.

One additional operational ask: can you confirm whether Brightline requires the export to include system-level telemetry (e.g., request logs) or only account-level user data payloads? If you need system telemetry we'll need to scope retention and pseudonymization accordingly.

I've also attached our current subprocessor roster (redwood_subprocessors_20261109.csv) for procurement review.

If these items look good to you, can procurement/legal confirm the Annex redline and we can move to DocuSign?

Thanks for the quick turnaround — aiming to get this signed before the end of the week.

Best,
Nikhil Sharma
